title: The Weight Atlas: Inside Weight-Space Programming - Living Change Log
description: Chronological tracking of empirical replications, community critiques, and monograph updates for Weight-Space Programming.
author: Het Patel (Hunterdii)

entries.title: Interactive Atlas Edition Launch & In-Browser Fingerprint Lab
entries.summary: Shipped the complete web platform with live in-browser Exp. 1 Atari weight fingerprinting, Prologue, 4 standalone Python labs, and interactive WSP-Bench-Lite scorecard.

entries.title: The Weight Atlas Edition Whitepaper (45 Pages)
entries.summary: Expanded scholarly whitepaper to 45 pages with 40+ original schematics, recomputed Exp. 1 agent weights, 54 verified citations with back-links, and full mathematical derivations.

entries.title: Andreas Maier: What is Measured and What is Anecdote
entries.summary: Independent academic audit catalogued claims into empirical evidence tiers: 3 Strong, 3 Moderate, 2 Weak. Highlighted missing direction-ablation baselines and n=1 seed limitations.

entries.title: Sean Goedecke: Deflationary Analysis on Weight Reading
entries.summary: Argued that reading weights is analogous to emitting raw assembly: an impressive spatial reasoning trick, but standard gradient training remains the primary tool for updating weights.

entries.title: Matthew Honnibal: Structural Separation of Methods
entries.summary: Clarified that only Exps 1, 2, and 4 read raw floats directly; all language model experiments employ Python code interpreters.

entries.title: Simon Willison: Laptop Replication of Exp. 1
entries.summary: Reproduced Exp. 1 weight reading on an offline laptop running Qwen 2.5 7B. Identified Breakout at 88% confidence in 52 minutes.

entries.title: Ahsen Khaliq Re-Evaluates Qwen Checkpoint
entries.summary: Verified MATH-500 jump from 7.9% to 48.1% using the published Hugging Face checkpoint (RikiyaT/Qwen3.5-0.8B-weight-space-programming).

entries.title: MIT CSAIL Publishes 'Sparks of Weight-Space Programming'
entries.summary: Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab report that LLMs can natively read, fix, and write neural network weights without gradient descent.
